CONFIDENTIAL 


Brnst Christian Johannes POLL 


© Ce Pee Bee Oe we eee O22 eOee wee eee 


Born at Hanover, Germany on June 11, 1895. 

Director of Economics and Doctor of Science (Self styled). 

States that during the War he was a Captain in the Uhlans 
and also that he was in the German Air Force (Richthofen 
Squadron). 

He is said to rave been employed at one time in the 
German Secret Service. 

In 1915 his name was added to the list of persons refused 
entry into the United Kingdom. 

in 1925 he entered India on a forged Dutch passport 
and is believed to have travelled in Afghanistan on a 
Swedish passport prior to that. POLL later stated in 
Singapore in 1928 that he had entered India on a Dutch 
passport because he had certain business deals to carry 
through in that country and he could not enter as a German. 
He was appointed sales manager of the “"Indo-German Trading 
Agency? Calcutta, which was managed by Arabindo Bose, an 
ex detenu. FOLL's connection with this man together with 
his previous record and the fact that he was known to be in 
touch with CRALIAR SALT Ae. @ well-known communist, led to 
the question of his deportation from India being taken up. 
POLL falsely stated that, although his mother was German 
and he had been brought up in Germany, his father was a 
Dutchman and he himself had been born at The Hague. However, 
this etatement was disproved by an application of his wife, 
Frau Alexandra Pauline POLL, for permission to enter India, 
which stated that her husband was by nationality @& Germait, 
and was German born. His apessport No. 7004 alse subse> 
quently showed that he was born in Gexrmamy. 

He firet came to notice im Singagere on Tame 2, aes, : 
where he was permitted te lend in transit for the Wetherlend 
Indies.

In August, 1926, A Mr. Demuth arrived in Bombay to take 
over the business POLL had been managing. A thorough 
examination of the books was made and Demuth came to the 
conclusion that it was a questionable concern and refused to 
be associated with it. He discovered thr* POLL had 
misappropriated considerable amounts of money belonging to the 
business, including the whole of the heavy monthly payments 
intended for advertisements. 

He appeared again in Singapore on September 28,1926, by 
the s.s. "Viminale.* He had intended to land in Colombo 
and to take ship to Gao but was refused admission by the 
Colombo Police. So he came on to Singapore and returned to 
Burope by the s.s. "Munsterland," on October 1,1926. 

He next arrived in Singapore by the s.s. “Saarbrucken® 
from Belawan on January,8,1928. He was then travelling on 
passport No. 7004, issued in Hamburg on March 14,1923. On 
that occasion he stated that he represented Krupp's Steel Works 
in Malaya, the Netherlands Indies and Saigon, and produced a 
business card which showed him to be Krupp’s representative. 

Xn Singapore he approached Namazie and Co., to do business. 
That company referred to the German Consul-General and was 
informed by the latter that POLL was not a representative of 
Krupp. The real representative of Krupp, who had come to 
hear of the matter, also repudiated him. POLL, in fact, came 
to Malaya as representative of a fixrm of brokers called 
Glaser and Pfrlaum, Berlin, which deals, among other things, 
in machinery. 

He visited Siam in March 1929, and stated on his return 
that he had supplied railway materials to the Siamese 
Gevernment. 

His business methods left much to be desired and many firms 
refused to have any dealings with him. 

On March 15,1932 POLL landed in Calcttta, having been 
issued a visa for India in error at Penang, where he had 
applied for the seme, knowing that he would be more likely 
to obtain one there than in Singapore where he was known.

He was then travellingon passport No. 10/28, issued by the 
German Consul-General, Singapore, on June 20, 1928. 

On March 24, 1933, POLL arrived at Southampton by the 
8.8. *AQuitania.*® He was refused permisaiion to land. Two 
days later, he arrived at Croydon by aeroplane and was 
again refused entry. At Croydon it was discovered that 
the renewal stamps from an Egyptian visa on his passport 
had been removed and stuck down again so as to cover the 
Southampton refusal stamp: the revenue stamps had been 
obliterated so as to continue on the page of the passport 
iteé@lf and the date January 13, 1933, and some pseudo~-Arabic 
hieroglyphics with initials added. 

POLL procures orders for machinery in Malaya, Nether=- 
lands Indies and Saigon for several firme in Germany. He 
is known to have represented,besides Messrs. F. C. Glaser 
and R. Pflaum of Berlin, the following firms:- 

Messrs. Demag, Deusberg - (Said to have lost agenéy in 1934) 

Messrs. Stahlwake Roochling-Buderus, A.G. of Wetzlar. 

Messrs. Aleverzee Handgeschellschaft ,M.B.H., Dusseldorf, 
Uhlandstrasse, 58. 

He is also interested in exporting pineapples. 

On July 25, 1935, POLL attempted to cheat one Kok Hung, 
the Chinese manager of Sungei Besi Mine, over a deal in exe 
cavators. After this affair, POLL is reported to have in- 
gratiated himself with the German Consul-General, who has 
since described POLL as “a bluffer,*but has not committed 
himself further. On July 31, 1935, G. Seefeld, 117-3,

claim to the agency for the "German Tube Syndicate.® 

POLL returned to Singapore by the s.s. "Gneisenau" on 
January 31, 1936, and was refused readmission to Malaya. 

He was, however, allowed te land for fourteen days, as am 
®alien in transit" in order to wind up his affairs.

Date September 8, 1936.

Subject Movements of E. C. J. Poll.

Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by J. Bryn D S I

With reference to the expected arrival of Ernst Christian
Johannes Poll, information has been received from the Boarding
House Section that this individual arrived in Shanghai on
board the s.s. Empress of Canada on April 5, 1936.
This information was verified at the Chinese Passport
Examination Bureau in Avenue Edward VII.
According to the Alien Passport Examination Form filled
in by Poll, he travelled here from Canton via Hongkong on
Passport I/R/22/33 issued at Berlin on May 23, 1933 and
visaed on February 8th at Singapore. He indicated that the
object of his trip here was one of business, and gave 4 to 6
weeks as the probable length of his sojourn in this city.
Since April 5, 1936, the day of his arrival, Poll has
been staying at the Cathay Hotel, except during the period
July 21st to September 2nd, when he settled his bill and left
for a holiday in Tsingtao.
Poll represents himself to be an agent for the Austrian
firm of car manufacturers known as "STEYR." He receives
letters from this company addressed to the hotel. So far as
is known he has no business office in town.

（批：file / Adolph）
Copy to 'B'
9/9
（签名：D.S. Jones）
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

日期 1936年9月8日。

主题 E. C. J. Poll 的行踪。

制作人 D.S. Jones 转呈人 J. Bryn D S I

关于 Ernst Christian Johannes Poll 预期抵达一事，已从寄宿公寓组收到情报，称此人于1936年4月5日乘坐“加拿大皇后”号轮船（s.s. Empress of Canada）抵达上海。
该信息已在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的中国护照查验局得到核实。
根据 Poll 填写的外国人护照查验表，他持1933年5月23日在柏林签发、2月8日在新加坡签证的 I/R/22/33 号护照，经香港从广州来此。他表示此次来沪目的是商务，并称在本市停留时间可能为4至6周。
自1936年4月5日抵达之日起，Poll 一直住在华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel），但在7月21日至9月2日期间除外，当时他结清账单并前往青岛度假。
Poll 自称是奥地利汽车制造公司“STEYR”的代理商。该公司有寄往该饭店给他的信件。据所知，他在市内没有办公地点。

（批：归档 / Adolph）
抄送‘B’组
9/9
（签名：D.S. Jones）
D. S.

特科主管警官。

Subject (in full) E. C. J. Poll - inquiry from H.B.M. Consulate General.

Made by D. S. Jones Forwarded by D. S. J. Jones

SD copy
filed S.

The attached copy of a supplement to the Straits
Settlement Police Journal concerning a German named Ernst
Christian Johannes Poll no longer being required by H.B.M.
Consulate-General, I attach it to this report for purpose of
record.

Following receipt of information that Poll had left
Hongkong for Shanghai on April 7th, enquiries were made at
all shipping companies operating vessels which had sailed
from Hongkong on or about that date, in order to ascertain
whether or not Poll had booked a passage to Shanghai. Poll's
name, however, did not figure on the different passenger lists
examined. It was learned later that Poll had not left
Hongkong on the date indicated, and that so far as is known,
he is there yet.

Particulars of this man have been noted and should it
later be discovered that he has either arrived in Shanghai
or passed through, a further report, giving whatever additional
details regarding him are obtainable, will be submitted.

制作人 D. S. Jones 转呈人 D. S. J. Jones

已归档 S.

随附一份《海峡殖民地警察期刊》增刊的副本，内容涉及一名名为 Ernst Christian Johannes Poll 的德国人，因英国驻华总领事馆不再需要该资料，故将其附于本报告以备存档。

在收到 Poll 已于4月7日离开香港前往上海的消息后，向所有在该日期左右从香港启航的轮船公司进行了查询，以查明 Poll 是否预订了前往上海的船票。然而，在查阅的不同乘客名单中并未出现 Poll 的名字。后来得知，Poll 并未在所述日期离开香港，且据所知，他目前仍在那里。

此人的详细情况已记录在案，若日后发现他已抵达上海或途经此地，将提交进一步报告，提供所能获得的关于他的任何额外细节。

CONFIDENTIAL

Ernst Christian Johannes POLL
------------------------------------

Born at Hanover, Germany on June 11, 1895.

Director of Economics and Doctor of Science (Self styled).

States that during the War he was a Captain in the Uhlans
and also that he was in the German Air Force (Richthofen
Squadron).

He is said to have been employed at one time in the
German Secret Service.

In 1915 his name was added to the list of persons refused
entry into the United Kingdom.

In 1925 he entered India on a forged Dutch passport
and is believed to have travelled in Afghanistan on a
Swedish passport prior to that. POLL later stated in
Singapore in 1928 that he had entered India on a Dutch
passport because he had certain business deals to carry
through in that country and he could not enter as a German.
He was appointed sales manager of the "Indo-German Trading
Agency," Calcutta, which was managed by Arabindo Bose, an
ex detenu. POLL's connection with this man together with
his previous record and the fact that he was known to be in
touch with Chattopadhyaya, a well-known communist, led to
the question of his deportation from India being taken up.
POLL falsely stated that, although his mother was German
and he had been brought up in Germany, his father was a
Dutchman and he himself had been born at The Hague. However,
this statement was disproved by an application of his wife,
Frau Alexandra Pauline POLL, for permission to enter India,
which stated that her husband was by nationality a German,
and was German born. His passport No. 7004 also subsequently showed that he was born in Germany.

He first came to notice in Singapore on June 26, 1936,
where he was permitted to land in transit for the Netherland
Indies.

《海峡殖民地警察特科政治情报期刊》摘录 - 1936年第2号增刊。

机密

Ernst Christian Johannes POLL
------------------------------------

1895年6月11日出生于德国汉诺威。

经济总监及理学博士（自称）。

声称战争期间曾任乌兰骑兵团（Uhlans）上尉，并称曾在德国空军（里希特霍芬中队）服役。

据说他曾受雇于德国秘密情报机构。

1915年，他的名字被列入拒绝进入英国的人员名单。

1925年，他持伪造的荷兰护照进入印度，并相信在此之前曾持瑞典护照在阿富汗旅行。POLL 后来于1928年在新加坡称，他持荷兰护照进入印度是因为他在该国有一些商业交易要完成，而作为德国人他无法入境。他被任命为加尔各答“印德贸易代理行”（Indo-German Trading Agency）的销售经理，该行由前被拘留者 Arabindo Bose 管理。POLL 与此人的关系，加上他之前的记录以及已知他与著名共产主义者 Chattopadhyaya 有联系的事实，导致其被驱逐出印度的问题被提上议程。POLL 虚假陈述称，虽然他的母亲是德国人，他在德国长大，但他的父亲是荷兰人，他自己出生在海牙。然而，这一说法被他妻子 Frau Alexandra Pauline POLL 申请进入印度的许可所驳斥，该申请指出其丈夫国籍为德国，且在德国出生。他的7004号护照随后也显示他出生于德国。

他首次引起注意是在1936年6月26日的新加坡，当时他被允许过境登陆前往荷属东印度。

in machinery.

He visited Siam in March 1929, and stated on his return
that he had supplied railway materials to the Siamese
Government.

His business methods left much to be desired and many firms
refused to have any dealings with him.

On March 15,1932 POLL landed in Calcutta, having been
issued a visa for India in error at Penang, where he had
applied for the same, knowing that he would be more likely
to obtain one there than in Singapore where he was known.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

1926年8月，一位 Demuth 先生抵达孟买，接管 POLL 一直管理的业务。经过对账簿的彻底审查，Demuth 得出结论认为这是一家可疑的企业，并拒绝与其发生关联。他发现 POLL 挪用了属于该企业的大量资金，包括原本用于广告的全部巨额月度付款。

他于1926年9月28日再次出现在新加坡，乘坐“维米纳莱”号轮船（s.s. "Viminale"）。他原计划在科伦坡登陆并乘船前往高阿（Gao），但被科伦坡警方拒绝入境。于是他继续前往新加坡，并于1926年10月1日乘坐“明斯特兰”号轮船（s.s. "Munsterland"）返回欧洲。

他下一次于1928年1月8日乘坐“萨尔布吕肯”号轮船（s.s. "Saarbrucken"）从贝拉湾（Belawan）抵达新加坡。当时他持有1923年3月14日在汉堡签发的7004号护照。在那次，他声称代表克虏伯钢铁厂（Krupp's Steel Works）在马来亚、荷属东印度和西贡开展业务，并出示了一张显示他是克虏伯代表的名片。

在新加坡，他接触 Namazie 公司洽谈业务。该公司向德国总领事馆查询，后者告知 POLL 并非克虏伯的代表。真正的克虏伯代表听闻此事后，也否认与他的关系。事实上，POLL 是作为一家名为 Glaser and Pflaum 的柏林经纪公司的代表来到马来亚的，该公司经营机械等业务。

他于1929年3月访问暹罗，回国时称已向暹罗政府供应铁路材料。

他的商业手段令人不敢恭维，许多公司拒绝与他有任何往来。

1932年3月15日，POLL 在加尔各答登陆，他在槟城错误地获得了印度签证，他明知在新加坡因其名声在外很难获得签证，而在槟城则更有可能获得，故在此申请。

pages.en:
- 3 -

He was then travellingon passport No. 10/28, issued by the
German Consul-General, Singapore, on June 20, 1928.

On March 24, 1933, POLL arrived at Southampton by the
s.s. "Aquitania." He was refused permission to land. Two
days later, he arrived at Croydon by aeroplane and was
again refused entry. At Croydon it was discovered that
the renewal stamps from an Egyptian visa on his passport
had been removed and stuck down again so as to cover the
Southampton refusal stamp: the revenue stamps had been
obliterated so as to continue on the page of the passport
itself and the date January 13, 1933, and some pseudo-Arabic
hieroglyphics with initials added.

POLL procures orders for machinery in Malaya, Nether-
lands Indies and Saigon for several firms in Germany. He
is known to have represented, besides Messrs. F. C. Glaser
and R. Pflaum of Berlin, the following firms:-

Messrs. Demag, Deusberg - (Said to have lost agency in 1934)
Messrs. Stahlwerke Roechling-Buderus, A.G. of Wetzlar.
Messrs. Aleverzee Handgesellschafft,M.B.H., Dusseldorf,
Uhlandstrasse, 58.

He is also interested in exporting pineapples.

On July 25, 1935, POLL attempted to cheat one Kok Hung,
the Chinese manager of Sungei Besi Mine, over a deal in ex-
cavators. After this affair, POLL is reported to have in-
gratiated himself with the German Consul-General, who has
since described POLL as "a bluffer,"but has not committed
himself further. On July 31, 1935, G. Seefeld, 117-B,
Meyer Flats, 37, Philip Street, Singapore, repudiated POLL's
claim to the agency for the "German Tube Syndicate."

POLL returned to Singapore by the s.s. "Gneisenau" on
January 31, 1936, and was refused readmission to Malaya.
He was, however, allowed to land for fourteen days, as an
"alien in transit" in order to wind up his affairs.

POLL is at present travelling on passport No. S.R.
72/33 issued at Berlin on May 25, 1933. He left for Bangkok
by train on February 14, 1936.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

当时他持有1928年6月20日由新加坡德国总领事馆签发的10/28号护照。

1933年3月24日，POLL 乘坐“阿奎塔尼亚”号轮船（s.s. "Aquitania"）抵达南安普敦。他被拒绝登陆。两天后，他乘飞机抵达克罗伊登（Croydon），再次被拒绝入境。在克罗伊登，人们发现他护照上埃及签证的延期印章被揭下并重新粘贴，以覆盖南安普敦的拒签印章；印花税票被涂改，以便在护照本页面上继续使用，并添加了1933年1月13日的日期以及一些带有首字母缩写的伪阿拉伯象形文字。

POLL 为德国的几家公司在马来亚、荷属东印度和西歌获取机械订单。已知除了代表柏林的 F. C. Glaser 和 R. Pflaum 先生外，他还代表以下公司：

Demag, Deusberg 先生们 - （据说于1934年失去代理权）
韦茨拉尔（Wetzlar）的 Stahlwerke Roechling-Buderus, A.G. 先生们。
杜塞尔多夫 Uhlandstrasse 58号的 Aleverzee Handgesellschafft, M.B.H. 先生们。

他对出口菠萝也感兴趣。

1935年7月25日，POLL 试图在一笔挖掘机交易中欺诈 Sungei Besi 矿场的华人经理 Kok Hung。此事之后，据报道 POLL 讨好了德国总领事，后者此后形容 POLL 为“一个吹牛者”，但未作进一步表态。1935年7月31日，居住在新加坡菲利普街37号 Meyer 公寓117-B室的 G. Seefeld 否认了 POLL 声称拥有“德国管材辛迪加”（German Tube Syndicate）代理权的说法。

POLL 于1936年1月31日乘坐“格奈森瑙”号轮船（s.s. "Gneisenau"）返回新加坡，并被拒绝再次进入马来亚。然而，他被允许以“过境外国人”身份登陆十四天，以处理其事务。

POLL 目前持有1933年5月25日在柏林签发的 S.R. 72/33 号护照。他于1936年2月14日乘火车前往曼谷。

pages.en:
CONFIDE[
"Very plausible type of person - Spy? -
Lots of funds - Always about with women -
Claims to be Krupps' Representative (bluff) -
No criminal record - 1 to 1½ years since he
was in Singapore - Invariably tries to get
friendly with Army Officers and their wives."

Further information may be obtained
by writing confidentially direct to the
Criminal Investigation Department, Secret
Service Branch in Singapore.

FILE

pages.zh:
机密[
“非常 plausible（看似合理）的一类人 - 间谍？ -
资金充足 - 总是与女性在一起 -
声称是克虏伯代表（虚张声势） -
无犯罪记录 - 距上次在新加坡已有1至1½年 -
一贯试图与军官及其妻子建立友好关系。”

如需更多信息，可直接写信至新加坡刑事调查处秘密情报股，信件需保密。
